title: Behaviours: why rebalancing feels wrong
objectives: Answer five client behaviours with the manual's “what to say” line.
Explain why the rule is agreed in writing at the start.
body_md:
Rebalancing asks the client to do the opposite of what feels natural: sell what is doing well and buy what is doing badly. Expect pushback.

| Behaviour | What it sounds like | What to say |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Letting winners run | “Why sell equity when it's doing so well?” | “We're only trimming back to the mix you chose. You still hold 60% in equity.” |
| Fear of buying after a fall | “Why put more into something that's falling?” | “This is the rule we agreed while things were calm. It buys at lower prices, without guessing the bottom.” |
| Recency bias | “Debt has done nothing; let's drop it.” | “Debt is what we use to buy equity after a fall. It earns its place in bad years.” |
| Regret | “Last time we rebalanced, equity kept rising.” | “Rebalancing controls risk; it isn't a forecast. Some years it costs a little, some years it saves a lot.” |
| Inertia | “Let's leave it; it's fine.” | “Left alone, a 60% target became 70% in our 10-year example. Let's keep the risk you chose.” |

Tip: agree the rebalancing rule in writing when the client first invests. Later, you're following the client's own decision, not asking them to make a new one under pressure.
example: “Why sell equity when it's doing so well?” → “We're only trimming back to the mix you chose. You still hold 60% in equity.”
say: Agree the rule in writing when the client first invests.
Later, you're following the client's own decision.
never: Let the client decide under pressure each time.
Sell winners because they did well.

check.q: After a strong year, Rohan's 60/40 portfolio is at 68/32 and he doesn't want to sell equity. What do you do?
o: Explain the band was breached; use new money first, then a partial switch or STP; check loads and tax; record his decision
check.why: Explain the band was breached; use new money first, then a partial switch or STP; check loads and tax; record his decision.

check.q: Leela's 60/40 is at 50/50 after a sharp fall and she wants to wait. What do you say?
o: Remind her of the agreed rule; explain buying lower without predicting the bottom; consider staging the move; no market predictions
check.why: Remind her of the agreed rule; explain buying lower without predicting the bottom; consider staging the move; no market predictions.

check.q: After equity falls, rebalancing can mean:
check.why: Restoring the target buys the underweight asset.
